answer: Reversible identity lien: each new identity posts a lien tied to a real-world operator account, and any confirmed sybil cluster freezes the operator's entire lien pool by dawn. Because the lien is shared across all identities an operator controls, one detection event costs the attacker every deposit at once rather than one wallet's stake. As the sybil tide rises, detection latency shrinks, so the expected cost per fake identity climbs faster than the number of identities. Honest operators stay above the reef because their liens are never pooled with fakes.
